title: Thread confinement
points: Thread confinement partitions the data so each piece is owned and touched by only one thread, so no lock is needed on it.
Typical form: route work by key (e.g. hash of seat or account id) to a dedicated single-threaded worker or queue.
It suits machine-triggered, high-throughput load where lock contention is the concern.
It only works if you can partition by thread; work that spans partitions needs coordination.
trade: Use when contention is high and data partitions cleanly by key. Versus fine-grained locks: no lock overhead or deadlock, but you need routing and cross-partition operations are hard. Same idea as one-thread-per-shard designs (e.g. a single-threaded event loop).
test: A machine-driven stream of millions of booking events per second hits seats that can be keyed by id. Locks are a bottleneck. What do you do?
answer: Thread confinement: hash each seat id to a dedicated single-threaded worker so one thread owns each seat and no lock is needed.

questions.question: How does thread confinement avoid locks?
options: It uses CAS on every field
Each partition of data is only ever accessed by one thread
It copies data on every read
questions.explanation: If a single thread owns the data, nothing races on it.

questions.question: When is thread confinement the best fit?
options: High-throughput machine-triggered load that can be partitioned by key
questions.explanation: It targets contention at scale and requires a clean partition. A counter wants an atomic, read-mostly data a read-write lock.
